transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to hold onto my thoughts anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words and numbers just scatter. I lose my place and can’t get it together.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with your thinking and concentration?
About three weeks now. It started after my older sister died.
Aside from the difficulties focusing, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time over these past three weeks?
Yes. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Even when my wife is being kind and talking to me, I feel like I’m down at the bottom of a well.
Over these past few weeks, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?
Yes. I haven’t touched the wood pieces on my bench, and I’ve skipped choir planning and chess. Even fishing sounds like more effort than it’s worth, which is really not like me.
Have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or guilt about yourself?
I’m not sure I’d call it that. I just feel very low, but I haven’t really been thinking of myself as worthless.
How has your sleep been over the past three weeks?
I’m not really sure what to say about that. I haven’t paid close attention to my sleep, honestly.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels, such as feeling constantly fatigued or drained?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular change in my energy.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or eating habits over the past few weeks?
Yes. Food just doesn’t appeal to me much lately. I’ll push breakfast around on the plate, and by supper my wife is reminding me I’ve barely eaten anything all day.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to die, or thoughts that you might be better off dead?
Yes... I keep thinking my family might be better off without me. And when I’m near the workshop, I get scared about where those thoughts could go if I were there alone.
